articles.title: ReBlade: The Death Spiral First Preview – Parrying Through the Cyberpunk Roguelite
articles.summary: With an eye-catching setting and seriously satisfying combat and parry action, developer ChillyRoom's cyberpunk roguelite concept shows solid promise as an action-RPG.
articles.body:
The demo we played shows promise, but we’re hoping for more depth in the final version.

The concept feels like a mix of Alita: Battle Angel and Cyberpunk 2077.

No other gameplay maneuver has had as much impact on modern action games as the parry. This ultimate skill suits both aggressive and defensive playstyles, letting you stylishly tip the scales of battle unscathed. Games like Sekiro, Lies of P, and the recent Onimusha: Way of the Sword lean into that focused combat style action fans have embraced. The upcoming ReBlade: The Death Spiral looks set to join that growing catalog of top-level action games that give you the tools and the satisfaction of tearing through enemies' defenses – this time within the framework of a roguelite.

Developer ChillyRoom has created a blend of a dungeon-crawling roguelite and fast-paced action-brawler, which leans into the idea of a cunning cybernetic warrior slashing and parrying through an ever-changing setting. In our hands-on with the ReBlade: The Death Spiral demo, we got to play over two hours of varied runs. This early hands-on made for a compelling onboarding experience for a stylish isometric roguelite action game, but we hope the full game shows much more of its core strengths in action.

ReBlade: The Death Spiral's core concept centers on the steady exploration of a far-future megacity steeped in the mystique of Chinese mythology. Set in a sprawling metropolis ruled by cyborg gangs and warlords reimagined as deities and mythological figures, you play a nameless android who crawls out of the trash heap, damaged but still ready for a fight. They soon chart a path of destruction across the ruthless neon city, aiming to stop the cycle of violence and uncover the truth of their origins.

The concept feels like a mix of Alita: Battle Angel and Cyberpunk 2077, offering a visually stylized, brutal world to cut a path through. It has all the trappings of a dystopian sci-fi thriller, making a solid and infrequently seen framework for a roguelite brawler. It focuses on the protagonist as they cut their path through the procedurally generated upper layers of the metropolis. Along the way, she'll collect new weapons with slick abilities like chain lightning and fire-burst damage, plus new chip modifiers that further buff her stats. She can even use her heightened cyborg strength to pull off cool finishers and kick bombs back at vulnerable foes.

All the familiar elements of an action-RPG roguelite are here, but the cyberpunk-style and setting, plus the focus on fast, parry-heavy brawler action gives ReBlade a different flavor and perspective than its contemporaries. However, the overall narrative, at least as far as I can tell from this demonstration, is fairly light. It mostly relies on vibes and environmental storytelling to sell the setting and the protagonist's motivations. That's not necessarily a major negative, and the visual style and tone certainly helps ground ReBlade. However, after several runs, it still left me wanting more context and reasons to invest in the journey.

ReBlade really puts its weight on the core action of its many runs. Starting in the lower rungs of the megacity, you fight everything from lowly machine drones to hulking bruisers lurking on different floors. The action flows akin to other isometric top-down action-brawlers like Hades, and it does a good job of conveying the fast pace of combat. Using combo attacks, sub-weapon skills, buffs, and that all-important parry, I cut my way past enemy defenses. Landing a series of deflects is very satisfying, and it's especially cool to rapidly deflect enemy blaster shots back at surrounding enemies. Seriously, it felt immensely fun to pull off lightning-fast parries like this one during my different runs.

ReBlade: The Death Spiral - First Screenshots

Even with the low-level gear you’re issued with at the start, ReBlade's combat fundamentals really do give you a sense of style and mastery when fighting enemies. I mostly stuck with the standard sword, which offers a balance of speed and power that I tend to favor, but I also had fun with the speedy twin blades and the heavier axe-and-shield combo. The action is further heightened by the more advanced weapons you'll find in dungeons and at various shops along the way. You can even swap certain buffs and perks between your gear to improve a favorite weapon found during a run. Tapping further into the cyberpunk angle, your protagonist can also augment themselves with different chips which add special modifiers to attacks, such as amplifying elemental damage or boosting recovery.

In an interesting change of pace from more linear roguelites, ReBlade lets you choose which path you want to take through its world. For each layer of the city, you're given choices about which areas to hit up, most of which are only available for a limited time before they disappear. This progression style let me focus on which weapon or performance upgrades and resource-gathering stages I wanted to pursue first. I really appreciated having a bit of choice in what loot I wanted, especially when I needed to save up cash before heading to one of the few shops that appear on the map.

ReBlade's combat really kicks into high gear during the boss encounters, which put the offense and defensive skills you've cultivated throughout a run to the test. These bosses blend cybernetic warlords and Chinese mythology, making the battles feel like the game is walking a fine line between a high-fantasy martial arts epic and a hard sci-fi action movie. I was really impressed by each boss's look and the design surrounding each battle; it delivered a showstopping finish to each layer. My favorite was a mysterious, wraith-like cyborg known as The Black, who fought like a cyber-enhanced grim reaper.

While I enjoyed ReBlade's spectacle and fast action, I found the demo sometimes felt a bit too generous. I didn't have much trouble getting through the two layers, especially when I found some great weapons that helped me clear enemies quickly. Moreover, you're also given a set of extra lives to help with runbacks on tougher challenges – which is very rare to see in a roguelite. While I like the ReBlade's focus on core action, I still felt some aspects of the roguelite structure were a bit underbaked and not fully realized as of this time, at least in this section of the game.

Still, this early demo offered some slick fights to dive into. With an eye-catching setting and seriously satisfying combat and parry action, developer ChillyRoom's cyberpunk roguelite concept shows solid promise as an action-RPG. While I hope ReBlade: The Death Spiral showcases a much deeper side in the full game, this early demo gets its stylized, grim world off to a solid start, and it's already got me ready to deflect and whittle down the cyborg opposition.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

Alessandro Fillari is a longtime games media professional. Talk video games with him on BlueSky at @afillari.bsky.social .

articles.title: Mads Mikkelsen, el nuevo villano de COD MW 4: ''Me gustaría llevar a The Archer a la gran pantalla"
articles.standfirst: El actor danés interpreta al gran villano de la nueva entrega de esta popular saga
articles.summary: El actor danés interpreta al gran villano de la nueva entrega de esta popular saga
articles.body: Uno de los grandes lanzamientos que tienen lugar en este mes de octubre de 2026 es sin duda Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4. La popular saga de videojuegos regresa con una nueva entrega en la que una de las grandes novedades es la aparición de Mads Mikkelsen, el reconocido actor danés, como nuevo villano. Desde MARCA Gaming recientemente tuvimos la oportunidad de viajar hasta Londres para una especie de estreno del juego. Allí además pudimos tener una pequeña charla con Mads Mikkelsen, que nos contó un poco más en profundidad algunos detalles sobre este nuevo personaje, The Archer, además de cómo es trabajar en la industria de los videojuegos. P. La primera pregunta que quiero hacerte es: ¿hasta qué punto es importante que un actor tenga una historia de fondo y una narrativa más profunda detrás del guion de un videojuego? Porque es diferente a una película. Y ¿hay algo que la experiencia de trabajar en una producción de videojuegos pueda enseñar a la industria cinematográfica? R. Creo que tener una historia de fondo siempre es importante para un actor, independientemente de lo que haga, ya sea teatro, cine o un videojuego. Si esa historia no existe realmente, te la inventas. La construyes junto con el director y puede que nunca llegues a hablar de ella, pero está bien tenerla guardada en la recámara. Pero en este caso había una historia muy larga. Era una historia muy desarrollada para mi personaje, así que eso fue todo un lujo. ¿Enseñarnos cosas mutuamente? Creo que, sin duda, podemos inspirarnos en los videojuegos cuando hablamos de cine, pero también pienso que ahora los videojuegos se están inspirando en las películas. Así que es algo mutuo, y creo que es positivo porque es el futuro. Es otra pequeña pieza del puzle que podemos unir a las demás. P. Eres el jefe final, el villano de este nuevo Call of Duty. ¿Qué nos puedes contar sobre este nuevo personaje? ¿Y te gustaría interpretar al héroe? R. Bueno, lo primero de todo es que no es un personaje nuevo. Creo que ha estado en las sombras todo este tiempo, y le haremos un guiño cuando oigamos hablar de él aquí. No lo veo como un villano. Siempre afronto mis personajes como personajes a los que tengo que intentar comprender de alguna manera. No necesariamente tengo que defenderlos, pero sí debo entender cuál es su propósito y cuál es su misión. Esa es mi forma de abordarlos. P. Imagina que llegas al final de este nuevo Call of Duty y te encuentras cara a cara con tu propio personaje. ¿Apretarías el gatillo o te lo pensarías dos veces antes de disparar? R. Bueno, ya me lo estoy pensando dos veces, ¿no? Eso casi me delata. Escuchemos lo que tiene que decir antes de disparar, ¿no? Eso es lo que puedo decir. P. Hay rumores y se lleva mucho tiempo hablando de una posible película de Call of Duty. ¿Crees que sería interesante que tu personaje apareciera en una película? R. Por supuesto. De hecho, me he enterado hoy mismo, así que sí, por supuesto. Creo que todo el mundo que ha formado parte de este proyecto, especialmente quienes han estado ahí desde el principio, merece una oportunidad de llevarlo a la gran pantalla. Al fin y al cabo, conocen a sus personajes mejor que nadie. Así que sí, sería divertido. P. Call of Duty presenta un conflicto ficticio, pero hoy cada vez parece más algo que podría suceder en el mundo real. ¿Quiénes o cuáles crees que son los tres villanos de la vida real, o jefes finales, a los que tenemos que derrotar en nuestra sociedad en este momento? R. Es una pregunta complicada. No, no diría personas. Quizá tres problemas de este mundo. Hay muchos problemas en el mundo. No creo necesariamente que estén más presentes ahora que hace 20, 40 o 60 años. Creo que siempre han estado ahí. Siempre hay conflictos entre ideologías y, a veces, simplemente permanecen dormidos. Después vuelven a salir a la superficie y todo termina estallando por completo. Supongo que hemos pasado por una fase en la que estaban medio dormidos, pero vemos cómo vuelven a asomar sus feas cabezas con demasiada frecuencia, diría yo.

articles.title: 'Haven't Played Your Console in a While?' Trade It in, Xbox Tells Customers Amid Stock Shortages
articles.summary: Xbox is sending emails to customers reminding them that they can trade in their Series X and S consoles if they’ve been collecting dust.
articles.body:
Xbox is sending emails to customers reminding them that they can trade in their Series X and S consoles if they’ve been collecting dust. The email has reportedly been sent to customers in the U.S. who haven’t used their console in some time.

The past year or so has seen console prices skyrocket thanks to the 'RAMpocalypse' sparked by generative AI companies such as OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft itself gobbling up components. As these AI companies vie for dominance and hoard all the RAM, prices soar for the end user while hardware is harder than ever to get hold of.

Valve’s Steam Frame VR machine was originally supposed to launch for $750 , for example, but thanks to the crisis created by AI companies, it ended up costing over $1,000. Meanwhile Nvidia graphics cards are way more expensive than they used to be.

Console price rises and shortages come at the worst time for both Sony and Microsoft, with November's launch of GTA 6 expected to spark a surge of interest in all things gaming. Given the game launches on console only, Rockstar's epic is sure to lead to a dramatic rise in PS5 and Xbox Series X and S sales. The only problem is, will Sony and Microsoft be able to meet demand?

With this in mind, you can see why Xbox would want people to hand over dormant consoles to new players. Here's what the email, verified by Windows Central , says:

“Haven’t played on your console in a while? If you’ve moved on to Xbox on PC or another way to play Xbox games, it may be time to trade in your console to Best Buy.”

This initiative was actually announced in June , when Microsoft said these consoles would be refurbished and resold at lower prices to make machines more readily available for customers. "We are working with retail partners on new programs to provide previously played consoles at lower prices," Microsoft said at the time. "Players who are ready to upgrade or no longer use their console will be able to trade it in with participating retail partners for cash or store credit. Those consoles will then be made available at lower prices for players."

The console hardware situation looks like it will get worse before it gets better. RAM manufacturers have reportedly sold their allocated memory capacity for 2027 already. The highest-end GPUs are near-impossible to get hold of unless you're willing to pay exorbitant amounts to a third-party seller.

articles.title: Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 Producer Explains Why This Season's Ending Is So Different From What Fans Expected
articles.summary: We sat down with Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2, who explained the ending of the anime’s second season and why it’s so tonally different from the first.
articles.body:
We sat down with Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 , who explained the ending of the anime’s second season and why it’s so tonally different from the first.

Warning: Major spoilers for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 below!

If you’re a Cyberpunk fan, you’re likely well-acquainted with the genre’s tragic overtones. This version of the future — a version toward which we seem to be hurtling faster and faster — isn’t a happy one, and it’s no surprise; with corpo technocrats stepping on the throats of world governments and the quality of life steadily decreasing in spite of massive technological advancements, it’s difficult to find a bright spot in the grimy worlds of Neo Tokyo, futuristic Chiba, and of course, Night City.

This was reflected perfectly in the heart-wrenching conclusion of Edgerunners’ first season , where basically everybody died and only one person got a ‘good’ — if heart-breakingly bittersweet — ending. When Edgerunners 2 was revealed, almost everyone anticipated another tear-jerking tale that would leave them feeling hollow at the end… but they couldn’t have been more wrong.

In a blessed turn of events, most of our main characters in Edgerunners 2 get a ‘happy’ ending of sorts. It’s definitely a stark turn from what most viewers expected, and I had to ask Sztybor why the team went in this direction when it’s a 180 from the groundwork that was previously laid in Season 1.

“Cyberpunk originated from noir, and in noir, there is always a character versus the city," he explained. "The main point is that you’ll never win with the city or the system. Even for me, Season 1 is not an obvious bad ending. For me, it is somehow, a happy ending. I think in the reality of pop culture we're living in, where those happy endings that we get in a lot of movies are super sweet, and ‘they lived happily ever after’ and all that, makes us think that all the endings from Cyberpunk or Edgerunners are bad endings, but maybe they are not.

“‘You are not destroying the bad corporation in the end.’ Yeah, well, that's not realistic, but you saved yourself, or managed to be who you are until the end, or you made this one choice, or you sacrificed for someone who you loved. And this is also somehow a happy ending, because you managed to stay true to your character until the very end. So I think, yes, it is a tragedy, but I think both noir and Cyberpunk are just trying to, I don't know, show us what real life is."

Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 is out now exclusively on Netflix. You can read our review here , where we scored it a 9 out of 10, saying it “delivers the gory, action-packed goods, even if it doesn’t quite hit the highs of its predecessor.” You can also check out our previous interview with Bartosz Sztybor, who explained why we don't actually get to see that much about Roman's personal life in this season.

Returning to Cyberpunk 2077 or playing it for the first time? We’ve got a new and improved Cyberpunk interactive map to help you find every mission, Iconic item, and collectible in the game. Plus, we’ve also got a full walkthrough for the base game, a Phantom Liberty walkthrough , and an overview of all the Cyberpunk 2077 endings so you don’t make a choice you regret. And we can’t ignore the various romance options you can smooch, which also impact how V’s story concludes.

articles.title: Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 Producer Explains Roman’s Backstory
articles.summary: I got the chance to ask Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2, all of my burning questions about the anime — particularly about one central character’s backstory (or lack thereof).
articles.body:
I got the chance to ask Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2, all of my burning questions about the anime's latest season — particularly about one central character’s backstory (or lack thereof).

Warning: Major spoilers for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 below!

Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 follows a totally different cast of characters from the show’s first season. One of these characters is named Roman, a young boy who loves all things retro and has a special affinity for old-school cinema. In fact, he loves traditional films so much that he carries around an old-school camcorder, which he uses to record the events around him in favor of the straight-to-your-cranium braindances (BDs).

Although we get a good glimpse at the tragedies that made our other main characters the way they are (Weak Kingsley, D, Talia Yang), Roman’s backstory is notably absent from the mix. And while he’s so young that it could be argued the events of this season basically serve as his backstory, there’s something that nagged at me the entire time I was watching: Why was his dad so permissive?

Maybe it’s my strict upbringing talking, but I was surprised to see how freely Roman’s father let him roam around Night City (even letting him bring D to his house on a few occasions). When asked about this, Sztybor revealed that, surprisingly, this wasn’t always the plan for Roman and his dad.

“He has things to do! He’s a barber and he trusts his boy,” he said of Roman’s father. “That was an artistic choice, not to explain too much. Roman is this glimpse of innocence in this weird, violent city, and walking happiness and trust and all that. I think that if you were to show his background… In our first draft of scripts, his dad had more dialogue with Roman, but we saw that it gave too much backstory to him. Then you start interpreting things, ‘Why is he this way?’

“I think it should be something for the audience that they just feel, ‘Okay, he’s that guy.’ You can, of course, start thinking and start creating his story and background, which is fine. I would say that telling too much about himself, his past, his family would destroy the feelings of who he is. This is the promise that I’m making, never in the Cyberpunk franchise will we show his backstory. It will be kept secret.”

I brought up my feeling that Roman was the lens through which we, the audience, watch the events of Edgerunners 2 unfold — and Sztybor acknowledged this take, while also revealing how he came to the conclusion of having a cinephile-type character being the central connecting thread to all of the other players in the story.

“The first pitch for Studio Trigger was, ‘I want to do an homage to the pop culture of the '90s. I want a pulp fiction kind of story with several characters that, at one point, connect.’ Working with Kai Igarashi, we discovered we are both cinephiles and we love cinema. We needed something, someone that connected all the characters, and if we were already doing an homage to pop culture of the '80s and the '90s — not just at the story level, but the visual level — then a cinephile kid would be a perfect choice. We thought this one innocent guy who loves retro, who is this glimpse of hope, and suddenly he’s the connection between all those flawed characters, would be an amazing choice.”

Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 is out now exclusively on Netflix. You can read our review here , where we scored it a 9 out of 10, saying it “delivers the gory, action-packed goods, even if it doesn’t quite hit the highs of its predecessor.”

Returning to Cyberpunk 2077 or playing it for the first time? We’ve got a new and improved Cyberpunk interactive map to help you find every mission, Iconic item, and collectible in the game. Plus, we’ve also got a full walkthrough for the base game, a Phantom Liberty walkthrough , and an overview of all the Cyberpunk 2077 endings so you don’t make a choice you regret. And we can’t ignore the various romance options you can smooch, which also impact how V’s story concludes.

articles.title: The Clash Royale Board Game Reaches Its Crowdfunding Goal in Less Than an Hour
articles.body:
Clash Royale: The Grand Arena has officially launched on Kickstarter and it's already off to a solid start. The upcoming board game adaptation has blown past its initial $25K goal in less than an hour after going live.

IGN had the chance to reveal the first trailer for the game last week and found it to be a faithful adaptation to the very popular mobile game. If you want to get in on the game before it officially launches, pledges start at $49 and go up from there.

This isn't the first Clash of Clans board game to come out of a collaboration between Maestro Media and Supercell. Clash of Clans: The Epic Raid followed a similar path via Kickstarter and managed to raise over $500K for the project ahead of its release. With the initial success of The Grand Arena, we expect the second board game adaptation to put up similar numbers before the campaign ends in November.

As for what the game actually looks like, we had the chance to talk to the game's lead designer, David Gordon about what actually went into its creation: “We tried mechanisms such as actual real time play against a clock, putting out a bunch of cubes, and simultaneous reveals, as well as various strategies to minimize the admin for players. Ultimately, we found that focusing on elixir spending in a turn-based card play system yielded a fun experience that most resembled that of the video game.”

the game itself, which is designed for 2-4 players, controls their own forces of eight-card decks built around a chosen Champion. Players take turns trying to destroy each other's towers, using elixir to fuel each move they make. Each tower you destroy earns you a crown, and the player with the most crowns at the end of the game is the winner.

“It was important that a strategy game fan who had never played the video game would find the tabletop version fun," said Gordon about the game. And that's really the core thesis behind and Clash of Clans game. You should be able to jump into gameplay fairly quickly and be able to have fun without knowing any backstory about the franchise.

Clash Royale: The Grand Arena is now available to support on Kickstarter . Fans can pledge their support via various tiers, including more expensive options that will get you access to expansions of the game.

Shrek 2 Remastered is real, and its release date is less than a month away.

As revealed during today's ID@Xbox showcase for October 2026, Aspyr Media has recreated a cult classic tie-in game from the original Xbox era for 2026. Shrek 2 Remastered is a modern version of Activision's co-op video game that will allow players to relive swampy memories when it comes to Xbox Series X/S next month, November 10.

The reveal trailer offers a sneak peek at how fan-favorite playable characters and classic moments from DreamWorks' fairytale sequel have been upgraded with improved graphics, new features, and more. It's been a while since players were able to play as Shrek, Fiona, Donkey, Gingy, and more, but you can get a taste of some of what's in store in the footage below.

You may have noticed that the opening isn't something from the original Shrek 2. Aspyr took today's announcement trailer as an opportunity to acknowledge the elephant in the room: That its November release date puts it within spitting distance of Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 . Set for release just nine days later, November 19, GTA 6 seems to have convinced most other games to steer clear of its launch window – but not Shrek.

The trailer takes a tongue-in-cheek jab at Rockstar's latest, going as far as to not only recreate its Vice City vibe but even come up with its own version of that iconic Grand Theft Auto box art, too.

The original Shrek 2 video game , meanwhile, launched in 2004 and came to the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and original Xbox. While we wait for the remaster to launch in just a few short weeks, you can check out a summary for the original experience below:

"Go beyond the film as you guide Shrek and all his pals on a thrilling, squad-based action-adventure for four players. Voyage through familiar haunts like Shrek's swamp. Tag-team baddies and use each character's special abilities to solve puzzles and accomplish mission objectives."

The Prestige stars Hugh Jackman, Christian Bale, Michael Caine, and Scarlett Johansson in a suspense tale about rival illusionists obsessed with becoming the greatest magician of all time, no matter what it costs them.

Nolan and his brother Jonathan Nolan (Fallout) penned the screenplay adaptation of Christopher Priest’s novel.

Produced by Emma Thomas, Aaron Ryder, and Christopher Nolan, The Prestige was nominated for two Academy Awards (Best Cinematography and Best Art Direction).

The Prestige ranks in third place in IGN’s picks for Christopher Nolan’s best films . In IGN’s The Prestige review , critic Todd Gilchrist awarded the film a 9/10 score, writing:

“Cinematic sleight-of-hand is a tough thing to pull off these days. No matter how secretive or sophisticated a filmmaker's approach might be, there are always folks savvy (not to mention cynical) enough to figure out what's happening long before any of their fellow filmgoers. articles.title: AMD FSR 4.1 Is Finally Coming to Xbox Series X, Rivaling PS5's QSSR
articles.summary: AMD FSR 4.1 has been a massive improvement for Team Red's AI upscaling tech, but it was previously only available on Radeon 7000 and 9000 graphics cards. But today, AMD has announced that the technology will now be coming to more devices, like the Xbox Series X.
articles.body:
AMD FSR 4.1 has been a massive improvement for Team Red's AI upscaling tech, but it was previously only available on Radeon 7000 and 9000 graphics cards. But today, AMD has announced that the technology will now be coming to more devices like the Xbox Series X.

Just like DLSS, FSR 4.1 uses AI to take a lower resolution input image and upscale it back up to native resolution, but because it's more computationally expensive than FSR 3, support for lower-powered hardware has been slow. However, thanks to the ongoing partnership with Sony (dubbed Project Amethyst), AMD has been making huge strides to make it run better on weaker devices.

AMD announced the widened support in a video , and will bring the upscaling tech to RDNA 2 graphics cards like the 6800 XT , along with Z2-powered handhelds like the Xbox Ally X20 . What stopped AMD from bringing this model to these older and less-powerful chips was that it was harder to run, which eliminated some of the benefit of even using upscaling. But, according to AMD SVP of Gaming and Graphics Jack Huynh, AMD was able to trim down the model to make it efficient on less powerful hardware that might not have the same suite of AI accelerators that RDNA 4 graphics cards do.

Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 – Hands-On Photos

This comes just a couple weeks after AMD and Sony did the same exact thing with PSSR 2 , trimming it down to a new model, dubbed QSSR , for the base PS5. QSSR does offer much better upscaling than FSR 2-based solution the PS5 had before, so I can only imagine this slimmer FSR 4.1 will have a similar effect for the Xbox Ally X.

But more importantly, this update will also allow FSR 4.1 to come to the Xbox Series X for the first time. The new upscaling model isn't out yet on Xbox, but AMD says it is 'coming soon,' although it's not clear what 'soon' means there. Hopefully, Microsoft is able to get it into a patch before Grand Theft Auto 6 launches next month.

After all, there have been plenty of concerns that Rockstar's next crime epic is going to be extremely hard to run for the base consoles , and a better upscaler just means better performance and improved image quality. But even if this FSR 4.1 update misses GTA's launch date, Xbox is going to continue working with AMD to bring upscaling to its consoles.

In the same video Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet confirmed that AMD's next-generation FSR 'Diamond' would be coming to Project Helix. And now that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has confirmed that Helix would be a whole 'family of devices,' I hope that this fancy new upscaling finds its way to all of them, no matter how powerful they are.

articles.title: Umamusume Fans Distraught After Los Angeles Concerts Canceled Due to Visa Issues
articles.summary: Umamusume concerts in Los Angeles have been canceled after workers could not get their visas approved in time for the event, leaving American fans distraught.
articles.body:
Two Umamusume concerts in Los Angeles have been canceled after workers could not get their visas approved in time for the event, leaving American fans distraught.

On October 18, the official Umamusume: Pretty Derby Twitter/X account announced that staffers working the shows — scheduled for October 22 and 23 — were having difficulties securing their travel visas. At the time, it did not cancel the events, but warned concertgoers that this may impact the festivities.

The possibility that these concerts would be canceled sparked concern among the game’s fanbase, with many joking (or perhaps being fully serious) that this event might politically “radicalize” them, given the extremely long wait times for visas in the United States right now.

The next day, Cygames confirmed that the Los Angeles concerts had been officially canceled, offering refunds to fans who’d purchased both on-site viewing tickets and streaming tickets to watch the show remotely. Responses to fans who made travel plans are also in progress, though Cygames admitted that this may take “some time.”

“Although we have coordinated repeatedly with all parties concerned and explored every possible option in our efforts to make this event happen, we were unable to obtain the necessary visas for entry into the US, so we have come to the painful conclusion that holding the concerts is no longer possible,” the post reads.

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass Reportedly Getting 'Major Overhaul,' Will Feature 'À La Carte' Options
articles.summary: Microsoft is reportedly planning a substantial revamp of Xbox Game Pass that will allow subscribers to choose the features they want in an à la carte fashion. The report comes by way of a new Fortune profile piece on Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.
articles.body:
Microsoft is reportedly planning a substantial revamp of Xbox Game Pass that will allow subscribers to choose the features they want in an à la carte fashion. The report comes by way of a new Fortune profile piece on Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

"Xbox is planning a major overhaul of Game Pass that would have players choose features à la carte," Fortune wrote, "including add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming, and multiplayer, with the system operating on a tiered structure, according to people familiar with the strategy."

The piece dug in on Xbox's controversial subscription gaming purchase, noting the challenges faced about the service internally: "Game Pass, a Netflix-style monthly gaming service, helped Xbox build a subscription business. But it also led to a cannibalization of sales for the company’s higher-priced first-party game titles, especially during the critical launch period. And competing internal metrics within different teams — such as subscription revenue versus store revenue — exacerbated the problem, said former employees."

Fortune's piece also addresses a next-gen Xbox handheld as well as the next-gen Project Helix console, suggesting that, as rumored, it won't be cheap — unless Microsoft chooses to subsidize any of the cost.

A Game Pass revamp would be only the latest in a series of bold moves by Sharma, who has been on the job barely six months and has already cut the price of Game Pass Ultimate, signed Hideo Kojima's next-gen Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor project Physint , started two new verticals within Xbox, and handed development of Halo to Activision , to name a few. She's even found time to personally respond to customer support tickets and check out the latest build of The Elder Scrolls 6.

articles.title: New Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles Artwork Answers the Biggest Question About This Epic Crossover
articles.summary: Marvel Comics has released a new preview for Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles, in the process answering the biggest burning question surrounding this unlikely crossover.
articles.body:
It's still hard to believe that Lucasfilm and Marvel Comics have actually done the unthinkable and greenlit a Star Wars/Marvel crossover . But that's exactly what we have to look forward to in January 2027, as Kevin Smith and David Marquez unite to give us Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles.

Marvel just released a new preview of the first issue of the series, and in the process they've addressed what may well be the biggest question surrounding the series. Check out this new art in the slideshow gallery below, and then we'll break it all down:

Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles #1 Preview Gallery

The burning mystery in question is whether the Marvel characters are aware of the existence of the Star Wars franchise in this story. After all, there's been a proud tradition of Marvel's heroes making tongue-in-cheek Star Wars references over the years, both in the comics and in the MCU. It would be a little weird if they suddenly behaved as if Star Wars isn't a thing in their home galaxy.

As this art shows, they clearly are aware of Star Wars, with every hero but Captain America being intimately familiar with the movies. Somehow, Star Wars has gone from being a beloved fictional property to a flesh-and-blood reality for the Avengers, and they're clearly more than a little taken aback at being thrust into the opening scene of Episode IV.

All of this suggests that Smith is taking a slightly more self-aware and fourth-wall-breaking approach to this particular crossover in his scripts. Are the lines between fiction and reality blurring together here, or will the series ultimately reveal that the Star Wars movies were always a true account of events that really did happen "a long time ago in a galaxy far, far away"? We'll find out in 2027.

Other big crossovers revealed this year have included Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars , G.I. Joe/Tomb Raider , and Batman/Superman/Weird Al: World's Weirdest.

articles.title: Fight Night, EA's Beloved but Long-Dormant Boxing Sim Franchise, Is Coming Back
articles.summary: Electronic Arts created social media accounts for its long-dormant boxing sim franchise Fight Night and the first post was exactly what fans wanted to hear: Fight Night is coming back.
articles.body:
Electronic Arts created social media accounts for its long-dormant boxing sim franchise Fight Night and the first post was exactly what fans wanted to hear: Fight Night is coming back.

The full post reads, "To everyone who stayed in our corner: Fight Night is coming back." And there's an image of a pair of boxing gloves hanging over a boxing ring with the caption, "The fight is never over." There are no additional details as of now, such as who's developing the project (the original and most recent two were built by EA Canada in Vancouver, while Fight Night Round 2 and Round 3 were developed by the now-shuttered EA Chicago), whether it's even a new game at all or potentially a remaster or remake – which I find unlikely given all of the licensing involved in these games; odds are it's a new entry – or a release window. Or, heck, if it's even targeting the current generation of consoles.

Regardless, the return of Fight Night should be welcome news to a lot of gamers, myself included. In the run-up to next month's 25th anniversary of Xbox, I've been writing a series of retrospective pieces about Xbox games I have fond memories of over the past quarter-century. One of those pieces was about Fight Night Round 3, which was, in my humble opinion, the first "holy sh*t!" game of the HD Era , graphically speaking.

While Fight Night has been dormant, EA has shifted its resources to the UFC game franchise, whose most recent entry, UFC 6, was released earlier this year and our reviewer thought it was great .

articles.title: Greta Gerwig Reportedly Clashed With Netflix Film Boss Over Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew
articles.summary: Barbie writer-director Greta Gerwig reportedly had a bitter falling out with Netflix’s then-head of film, Dan Lin, over her upcoming movie, Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew.
articles.body:
Barbie writer-director Greta Gerwig reportedly had a bitter falling out with Netflix’s then-head of film over her upcoming movie, Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew .

In their rundown of why Netflix fired Dan Lin earlier this week, Variety claimed Lin had clashed with both Gerwig and Ben Affleck (who most recently directed Animals for the streamer) during his tenure as the streamer’s movies boss.

“Four sources with knowledge of the matter said that, indeed, Lin and Gerwig had a falling out during a Zoom call about the project earlier this year. On a virtual meeting populated by numerous Netflix executives, Lin is said to have been ‘dismissive’ to the director in conversation about the progress of the film,” according to Variety.

“Lin is known in town to be incredibly fair, but at times obtuse in his frankness. Word travelled fast around Netflix that the meeting had gone south, at which point sources said [then-chief content officer Bela] Bajaria called Gerwig’s producer Amy Pascal to smooth things over. Two sources also said that Gerwig’s new, all-powerful CAA agent Bryan Lourd went to Sarandos directly over the faux pas. Lin was subsequently disappeared from the film, all sources concurred, and [Lin’s top lieutenant Doug] Belgrad stepped in as the primary Netflix exec overseeing the project (until, of course, he was laid off last week).”

“None of the sources suggested the incident led to Lin’s firing,” Variety added.

Not long before his firing, Lin declared in an interview that Netflix “just won’t work with” directors who want their films to also be released in cinemas . “There is a group of filmmakers who still want theatrical," Lin said. "Those are filmmakers that we’ve accepted we just won’t work with."

Netflix recently kicked off its marketing campaign for The Magician’s Nephew with the release of the first trailer and new poster for Gerwig’s film adaptation of C.S. Lewis’ 1955 fantasy novel.

That trailer was enough to convince IGN’s Jesse Schedeen to stop being skeptical about the project’s very existence .

Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew opens exclusively in theaters on February 12, 2027 (IMAX previews begin February 10) before streaming on Netflix on April 2.

The film’s cast includes David McKenna, Beatrice Campbell, Emma Mackey, Carey Mulligan, Ciarán Hinds, with Daniel Craig and Meryl Streep , Kobna Holdbrook-Smith, Denise Gough, Susan Wokoma.

articles.title: It Looks Like GTA 6's Beer Brands Are About to Become Real
articles.summary: It appears that Rockstar may be preparing to sell beer brands from GTA 6 in real life.
articles.body:
It appears that Rockstar may be preparing to sell beer brands from GTA 6 in real life.

As spotted by iGrandTheftAuto , labels for three GTA-related beer brands have been approved by the US Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau. The labels include brands that have been featured in previous GTA titles, such as Patriot Beer and Pißwasser (commonly known as Pisswasser). There's also a new brand known as No Mames Vice City, which features a little dog wearing sunglasses and a Vice City chain on the label.

These are being produced by a Florida brewery known as Tripping Animals Brewing. For alcohol afficianados, No Mames Vice City lager will have a 6% ABV, while the other two will be 4.2% ABV, which is identical to Bud Light's ABV. With all of that said, we have no idea exactly when or where these beverages will be sold.

They may be exclusive to bars in and around Miami, as Rockstar Games has completely taken over the city with GTA 6 ads . Citizens have spotted various in-universe ads for various GTA brands around the area, and there's also a giant Vice City blimp flying over Florida. The Miami Heat's arena has also been transformed ahead of an unprecedented Vice City-themed NBA game in November .

It's possible some of these drinks could be sold online, but it may make more sense to keep it limited to special in-person activiations around the city. Either way, it shows that Rockstar has spared no expense when it comes to alerting the public of GTA 6's arrival. Rockstar has also begun advertising the game in Paris, New York City, Chicago, and Los Angeles. It's unclear if any other cities will get big advertising outside of posters and billboards, or if this is all exclusive to Miami itself.

GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.
